evidence: paper: \mathcal{A} = \mathcal{A}_0 + \sum_{j\ge 1}\chi(a_j q)A_j,\qquad \mathcal{B}e_\theta = B_0 e_\theta + \sum_{j\ge 1}\chi(a_j q)B_j,\qquad p_{\mathrm{loc}} = p_0 + \sum_{j\ge 1}\chi(a_j q)p_j,\qquad u_{\mathrm{loc}} = \operatorname{curl}\mathcal{A} + \mathcal{B}e_\theta.

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Every piece of the display is in the Lean, in three respects differently packaged. (i) Index: the paper writes a free j = 0 block plus ∑_{j≥1} χ(a_j q)(·)_j, while potentialSum is one tsum over all j : ℕ whose j = 0 stage is the base/initialization block and is itself multiplied by χ(a_0 q). This is not a weaker statement: scaledCutoff is the bump with rIn = 1/2, so χ(a_0 q) = 1 whenever |a_0 q| < 1/2, i.e. the cut j = 0 term equals the uncut ℐ_0 near q = 0 (LocalPotentialRebundle.sum_eq_first uses exactly that hypothesis), and the paper's Step 1 explicitly permits cutting that block inside q < q_big. (ii) Grouping: the axial part of the base potential is moved out of ℐ into the direct angular field (LocalPotentialRebundle.potential / direct subtract and add removedPotential and its curl), so the Lean's A is not literally the paper's ℐ; velocity_eq_original states that curl A + D is unchanged by the move, which is what the display uses. (iii) Swirl: ℒe_θ is not a sum of vector stages B_j in the final statement but a single cylindrical scalar times e_θ (DirectAngularDiagonal.angularField b, with the stage sum selectedDirect shown equal to it by Properties.direct_angular). The last equality u_loc = curl ℐ + ℒe_θ is literally MixedPeriodicAssembly.velocity, instantiated as selectedRawVelocity and asserted for the constructed fields as Properties.decomposition. The constants a_j and the scale q are the same objects: (a j : ℝ) and PhysicalWaveSum.physicalQ ActualPrimary.h.
